rfi.title: Macron rallies government response as wildfires ravage south-west France
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron convened ministers on Monday before heading to south-west France, where wildfires have displaced hundreds of thousands and a new heatwave threatens to reignite the flames.

rfi.title: France and Spain battle vast wildfires as fresh heatwave approaches
rfi.description: Firefighters are continuing to battle huge forest fires across France and Spain on Monday, as authorities warned that another heatwave could bring temperatures of up to 40C to the already scorched wine-growing region around Bordeaux.

rfi.title: Threatened by fire, Bordeaux is 'ready for anything': mayor
rfi.description: The mayor of Bordeaux in southwest France said on Sunday authorities had no current plans to evacuate the UNESCO-listed city due to raging forest fires but were "ready for anything."

rfi.title: Paris police arrest man who wounded three women with knives
rfi.description: A French off-duty policeman on Monday detained a man after he allegedly attacked and wounded three women with two kitchen knives in Paris, France's interior minister said.

rfi.title: Niger’s junta marks three years amid rising violence and lost freedoms
rfi.description: Three years after President Mohamed Bazoum was overthrown, Niger is recording strong oil-driven growth but facing rising jihadist violence and a severe restriction of political freedoms, former ambassador Kiari Liman-Tinguiri tells RFI.

rfi.title: Ebola surges past 3,200 cases in DRC as Oxford begins first vaccine trial
rfi.description: The death toll from an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has climbed to 1,405, with confirmed cases now at 3,200, government data showed Sunday, as researchers race to develop a vaccine.

rfi.title: Iran halts retaliatory strikes as US gives diplomacy 'more room'
rfi.description: Iran and the United States have paused their attacks, offering Gulf shipping and global oil markets a respite after weeks of escalating strikes around the Strait of Hormuz.

rfi.title: Main suspect in Berlin Pride attack shot dead by German police forces
rfi.description: The suspect in the deadly Berlin Pride attack that left one person dead and 29 injured was shot and killed by police during a confrontation on Sunday in a suburb of the city, authorities said.

rfi.title: Tadej Pogacar wins a record-equaling fifth Tour de France title
rfi.description: Tadej Pogacar claimed his record-equalling fifth Tour de France title as Mathieu van der Poel won a sensational 21st and final stage around Paris on Sunday.

rfi.title: How slavery money built the Élysée, France’s presidential residence
rfi.description: What would become the Élysée Palace, the official residence of the French president, was built three centuries ago with a fortune amassed in the slave trade. As France grapples with its legacy of slavery, calls are mounting for the country to acknowledge this and other traces of the past.

rfi.title: Wildfire situation in France ‘remains very unfavourable’, interior minister says
rfi.description: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Sunday the wildfire situation in southwestern France was still "very unfavourable”. More than 300,000 people fled wildfires raging across France and Spain on Saturday as worsening conditions forced fresh evacuations.

rfi.title: UNESCO adds France's D-Day landing beaches, Greece's Mount Olympus to World Heritage List
rfi.description: UNESCO has added France’s D-Day landing beaches and Greece’s Mount Olympus to its World Heritage List, during a UN committee meeting in South Korea reviewing dozens of nominations.

rfi.title: Ecowas greenlights $25bn Nigeria-Morocco mega gas pipeline
rfi.description: West African leaders have approved plans for a gas pipeline linking Nigeria to Morocco, marking a major political milestone for one of Africa's most ambitious infrastructure projects.

rfi.title: No snakes in church and don't eat the frogs: the weird world of US animal laws
rfi.description: A few keywords in a search engine will bring up any number of strange laws involving animals in the United States. Many are urban myths: there is no law specifically prohibiting driving a car in Massachusetts with a gorilla in the back seat, although no one would dispute that would be a questionable idea. Others, however, are very real.

rfi.title: Trauma and taboos: how Portugal takes care of migrants' mental health
rfi.description: Migration is increasingly essential to Portugal's economy, but the mental health of many new arrivals to the country is affected by the trauma of what they have left behind, long and arduous journeys, and the racism that greets them, fuelled by far-right rhetoric. In addition, mental health treatment is often impeded by cultural and linguistic barriers.

rfi.title: Senegal ready to show ‘what it is capable of’ at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics
rfi.description: With venues nearing completion and public enthusiasm growing, Dakar 2026 chief organiser Ibrahima Wade tells RFI that Senegal is ready to make Olympic history when the Youth Games begin on 31 October.

rfi.title: Climate change 'exacerbating' drought across Europe, scientists say
rfi.description: Climate change is exacerbating drought in Europe as extreme heat evaporates water supplies, scientists said in a study published this week, with low water levels disrupting shipping, farming and industry in countries including Romania and Greece.

rfi.title: Iran seeks to 'sow confusion among Gulf states' by targeting Bahrain and Kuwait
rfi.description: As Iranian drones and missiles target Bahrain and Kuwait, RFI spoke with Mahdi Ghuloom of the Dubai-based ORF Middle East think tank, who believes long-standing tensions, the small size of the two countries and divisions over how the Gulf should respond are playing their part in this development.

euronews.title: UK's Burnham pledges full support to Ukraine in first meeting with Zelenskyy
euronews.description: Zelenskyy's visit was the first by a foreign leader since Burnham took office a week ago. The prime minister said it underscored the UK's "unwavering" support for Kyiv as it defends itself against Russia's full-scale invasion.

euronews.title: Ukraine keeps up long-range strikes on Russian export and oil facilities as pressure on Moscow builds
euronews.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his forces had struck an export terminal in the western Rostov region, as well as oil facilities in the Yaroslavl and Udmurtia regions far from the front line.

euronews.title: Gunther von Hagens, creator of exhibitions featuring preserved human corpses, dies at 81
euronews.description: Critics accused von Hagens of crossing into sensationalism with displays that included a corpse riding a plastinated horse and the body of a pregnant woman carrying an eight-month-old foetus.

euronews.title: 'Stored on racks': UK funeral director faces jail over uncremated bodies
euronews.description: The 48-year-old undertaker previously pleaded guilty to 67 offences spanning 12 years and affecting hundreds of victims.

euronews.title: Spain's wave of wildfires costs up to €3.275 billion in firefighting alone
euronews.description: The area burned in Spain in 2026 is almost half that of last year, putting firefighting costs at between 1.7 and 3.3 billion euros. Experts also warn of losses in tourism and farming and stress the need for prevention.

euronews.title: Why one smoker gets cancer and another doesn't: a study provides clues

euronews.description: Firefighters battle wildfires in central Spain as burned homes, cars and scorched landscapes reveal the devastation across Ávila province.

euronews.title: From Garpiya drones to a Starlink rival: Europe strikes at Russia’s military might
euronews.description: The EU’s latest sanctions package against Russia targets 56 military-industrial entities and individuals, including long-range drones and communication networks. Experts say the measures could bolster not just Ukraine’s battlefield efforts, but also Europe's future security.

euronews.title: Colombia's president-elect to close embassies in three European countries in diplomatic overhaul
euronews.description: Abelardo de la Espriella says he will cut diplomatic ties with Havana and Managua and close 15 consulates and 14 embassies to reduce costs and bolster security. The president-elect will be sworn in on 7 August in Cali.

euronews.title: Rabbis visit Qatar's emir for condolences in show of interfaith bonds
euronews.description: Following a meeting with Qatar's emir, Rabbi Mendy Chitrik of the Alliance of Rabbis in Islamic States said the delegation felt warmly welcomed and called for greater dialogue to strengthen Muslim-Jewish relations.

euronews.title: Tate brothers to remain in jail as they fight UK extradition
euronews.description: The Tates promote wealth, male dominance and misogyny through their social media empire and are among the world’s most polarizing internet personalities.

euronews.title: You can visit every bridge on the back of euro banknotes – and they’re all in one town
euronews.description: The original design wasn’t based on any actual bridges, but a town in the Netherlands decided to turn them into reality.

euronews.title: 'Out of capacity’: EU warns wildfires are pushing response systems to the limit
euronews.description: The European Commission has activated its emergency response system to support France and Spain as they battle wildfires. France has received seven firefighting aircraft and four helicopters, while Spain has been provided with six aircraft and three ground firefighting teams.

euronews.title: Masked performers fill Porto-Novo streets in Benin festival
euronews.description: Thousands gather in Porto-Novo for Benin's Mask Festival, celebrating ancestral traditions with colourful costumes, dances and masks.

euronews.title: Three injured in Paris knife attack, one suspect arrested, police say
euronews.description: Three women aged 19, 24 and 36 were taken to the hospital after the assault. The suspect's identity and motives are not immediately known.

euronews.description: The Culture Club frontman has released on new song, posted on his X account, in which he openly denies that a genocide is taking place in Gaza. The message of support contradicts reports from the UN and Amnesty International, and the online reaction to the track has been vitriolic.

lemonde.description: Le feu se rapprochait, dimanche, de la banlieue sud-ouest de Bordeaux, contraignant les pompiers et les volontaires à d’incessantes manœuvres à 15 kilomètres de la métropole girondine pour se redéployer et attaquer les flammes.

lemonde.title: « Je n’aurais pas cru que cela puisse se passer dans la ville la plus “queer-friendly” du monde » : Berlin bouleversée par l’attentat contre la Marche des fiertés
lemonde.description: Samedi soir, une femme est morte, et 29 personnes ont été blessées, après qu’un homme conduisant une camionnette a foncé sur un groupe de participants, dans le bois de Tiergarten. Après une longue cavale, le suspect, Abdul Ballout, a été abattu par la police, dimanche soir, dans le quartier de Spandau.

lemonde.title: Kirkenes, le petit port sur la nouvelle route de l’Arctique où grouillent les espions
lemonde.description: « La ruée sur les ports » (16/16). Le réchauffement climatique pourrait changer le destin de la petite ville norvégienne de 3 500 habitants qui se situe sur une nouvelle route maritime, libérée par la fonte de la banquise, reliant l’Europe et l’Asie. Mais la proximité de la Russie et les tensions géopolitiques contrarient ses ambitions.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : Donald Trump assure que les Etats-Unis disposent de suffisamment de munitions
lemonde.description: Dans une interview au « Wall Street Journal », le président américain a nié toute pénurie alors que des inquiétudes se font jour concernant les stocks américains d’intercepteurs antimissiles. D’après le Center for Strategic and International Studies, au moins 1 500 intercepteurs Patriot auraient été utilisés depuis le début du conflit, laissant moins de 1 000 unités dans les stocks américains.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : une attaque de drones ukrainiens fait deux morts dans le sud de la Russie, selon les autorités locales
lemonde.description: Une frappe ukrainienne nocturne sur la ville de Rostov-sur-le-Don a tué un couple et blessé cinq personnes, a déclaré le gouverneur régional. De son côté, l’armée ukrainienne a affirmé que 147 drones russes avaient été lancés contre le territoire ukrainien pendant la nuit, précisant que l’attaque se poursuivait lundi matin.

lemonde.title: Canicule : quand l’architecte des bâtiments de France s’oppose à une climatisation
lemonde.description: Si les maires ne peuvent passer outre un avis défavorable de l’architecte des bâtiments de France, le Parlement étudie néanmoins un allègement pour les protections solaires.

lemonde.title: La réouverture du musée Nissim de Camondo, à Paris, reportée à 2030
lemonde.description: Fermé depuis la fin de 2024, l’établissement, qui abrite l’une des plus belles collections d’art du XVIIIᵉ siècle, devait rouvrir à la fin de l’année, après un chantier d’un coût de 23 millions d’euros.

lemonde.description: Vainqueur de justesse de la dernière présidentielle, Abelardo de la Espriella avait reçu l’appui du président américain, Donald Trump, pendant la campagne.

lemonde.title: « L’IA repose sur une géographie concrète, mettant des territoires au service du calcul, selon une logique de comptoirs »

lemonde.title: A Antibes, sur la plage de Salis, l’imbattable pan-bagnat de Chez Josy

Sur la plage de la Salis, à Antibes, le cabanon Chez Josy perpétue la tradition du pan-bagnat maison, depuis soixante ans.

lemonde.title: En Inde, la mobilisation des « cafards », mouvement de contestation de la jeunesse, fragilise Narendra Modi
lemonde.description: Le premier ministre indien s’est décidé, samedi, à limoger son ministre de l’éducation, comme le réclamaient les étudiants depuis un mois. Cette jeunesse désenchantée, dont la frustration était longtemps restée étouffée, a sérieusement écorné l’image du dirigeant par son mouvement dépassant les classes sociales.

france24fr.description: Les États-Unis ont quitté, lundi, une réunion du Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU pour, selon eux, dénoncer des commentaires "hypocrites" de la France. Paris a comparé Washington à la Corée du Nord et à la Russie au sujet d'un vote lié aux droits humains, selon un représentant américain.

france24fr.title: Biens mal acquis : le PNF demande le renvoi de BNP Paribas et des enfants d'Omar Bongo

france24fr.description: Alors que les pompiers poursuivent leur lutte contre les flammes près de Lège-Cap-Ferret, un élan de solidarité s'organise sur le terrain. Agriculteurs, habitants et bénévoles apportent leur aide aux secours pour faire face à cet incendie hors norme.

france24fr.title: Non, rien ne prouve que la crème solaire augmente le risque de cancer
france24fr.description: Une étude menée sur plus de 470 000 personnes est utilisée sur les réseaux sociaux pour affirmer que la crème solaire augmenterait le risque de cancer de la peau. Mais l’étude en question ne portait pas sur la dangerosité des crèmes solaires et ses conclusions ont été largement déformées.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : "On va continuer à mener cette bataille" dit le président Macron en Gironde
Violence des colons en Cisjordanie occupée : Benjamin Netanyahu a "intérêt à enflammer la situation"
france24fr.description: Depuis vendredi, la Cisjordanie occupée connaît une nouvelle flambée de violences, après la mort de quatre Palestiniens et deux Israéliens. Benjamin Netanyahu y a annoncé une vaste opération armée et promis d'accélérer la colonisation. À trois mois des élections, un embrasement du territoire palestinien servirait-il le camp du Premier ministre ?

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : des soignants en grève à Bunia pour réclamer leurs salaires
france24fr.description: En RDC, des soignants ont manifestés samedi à Bunia, contre des mois de salaires impayés. Une mobilisation qui intervient alors que l'épidémie d'Ebola a déjà fait plus de 1 300 morts, selon le dernier bilan de l'OMS.

france24fr.title: France : une attaque au couteau fait trois blessés à Paris
france24fr.description: Une attaque à l'arme blanche dans le nord-ouest de la capitale française. Trois femmes ont été blessées, lundi 27 juillet à Paris, dont deux grièvement, et un homme, soupçonné d'être l'auteur de l'attaque, a été interpellé par un policier hors service de la préfecture de police. Les faits se sont produits vers 11 h 30 porte de Clichy, située dans le XVIIe arrondissement, au nord-ouest de la capitale, a indiqué la préfecture de police de Paris (PP).

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Javier Milei accuse le Brésil d’avoir financé une “campagne anti-argentine"
france24fr.description: Des tensions diplomatiques qui sont encore montées d’un cran entre le Brésil et l’Argentine. Ce dimanche 26 juillet, Javier Milei a accusé le Brésil d’avoir financé une “campagne anti-argentine”, faisant référence en partie aux critiques qu’ont subi l’équipe d’Argentine lors du Mondial 2026.

france24fr.title: Le mégafeu en Gironde "stabilisé" mais la reprise redoutée
france24fr.description: Le mégafeu aux portes de Bordeaux qui a ravagé 42.000 hectares est "stabilisé" mais pas "fixé", selon le ministre de l'Intérieur, et les pompiers, après une nuit pluvieuse et une "accalmie" des conditions météorologiques, font face à une remontée des températures qui laisse redouter une reprise de l'incendie, avec jusqu'à 40°C attendus mardi. "Demain la situation s'annonce plus compliquée puisque les températures vont augmenter (...) et la météo annonce plus de vent", rapporte notre journaliste

france24fr.title: Attaque en mer Caspienne : l'Iran met en garde l'Ukraine contre des conséquences "imprévisibles"
france24fr.description: L'Iran a mis en garde l'Ukraine lundi 27 juillet contre des conséquences "imprévisibles" après l'attaque, ce week-end, d'un de ses navires en mer Caspienne, attribuée à Kiev. Le décryptage de notre chroniqueur international Gauthier Rybinski.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : pourquoi Kiev cible les entrepôts de Wildberries, l'"Amazon russe"
france24fr.description: Depuis le 18 juillet, l’Ukraine multiplie les bombardements visant les entrepôts de Wildberries, l’équivalent russe d’Amazon. Avec ces attaques, Kiev veut rappeler à la population russe que le conflit a un impact immédiat sur les civils, et par la même occasion viser un groupe russe accusé de soutenir l’effort de guerre du Kremlin.

france24fr.title: Trump laisse "de la place" aux négociations avec l'Iran, selon son ambassadeur à l'ONU
france24fr.description: Donald Trump laisse "de la place" pour des pourparlers avec l'Iran, selon son ambassadeur à l'ONU, après une accalmie des frappes américaines. Alors que la guerre dure depuis bientôt cinq mois, la presse américaine fait état d'un possible manque de munitions.

france24fr.title: Maroc : coup d’envoi de la CAN féminine 2026
france24fr.description: La CAN féminines 2026 a débuté ce dimanche au Maroc. Pendant trois semaines, seize équipes vont tenter de décrocher le titre continental.

france24fr.title: L'Arabie saoudite accuse des groupes pro-iraniens après une attaque de drones depuis l'Irak
france24fr.description: L'armée saoudienne a intercepté et détruit plusieurs drones lancés depuis l'Irak et visant des installations pétrolières, a indiqué lundi le ministère de la Défense, accusant des groupes armés soutenus par l'Iran. L'attaque intervient malgré l'accalmie observée entre les États-Unis et la République islamique, après 13 jours d'affrontements d'affilée.

france24fr.title: "On n'a pas fini de jouer ensemble" : une lettre aux Français et une promesse de Mbappé
france24fr.description: Une dizaine de jours après la piteuse fin de Coupe du monde de l'équipe de France contre l'Angleterre, le capitaine des Bleus, Kylian Mbappé, a pris la parole. À l'heure des réseaux sociaux, il a préféré écrire une lettre ouverte aux Français, publiée dans la presse, pour remercier les supporters.

france24fr.title: Tchad : première édition du semi-marathon de  N'Djamena pour la Paix
france24fr.description: Au Tchad, plus de 700 coureurs ont participé ce dimanche au premier semi-marathon pour la Paix à N'Djamena. 17 nationalités étaient représentées. L'événement se veut un appel à l'apaisement, dans un contexte marqué par les récentes tensions dans le pays.

zeit.title: 150 Jahre Festspiele: Gemischte Reaktionen auf Bayreuther KI-«Rheingold»
Schüsse in Seattle: Polizei in Seattle nimmt nach tödlichen Schüssen 15-Jährigen fest
zeit.description: Nach tödlichen Schüssen auf einem Food-Festival in Seattle hat die Polizei einen Jugendlichen festgenommen. Ein weiterer Verdächtiger ist offenbar noch auf der Flucht.

zeit.title: Platzverweise: Radfahrer missachtet Rot - Zusammenstoß mit drei Fußgängern
Transfers: Hoffenheim verleiht Orban in die Türkei
Waldbrände in Frankreich: Emmanuel Macron ruft wegen heftiger Waldbrände zum Zusammenhalt auf
zeit.description: Frankreichs Präsident besucht das Waldbrandgebiet im Westen des Landes. Dabei spricht er Einsatzkräften und der Bevölkerung Mut zu: »Wir werden diesen Kampf gewinnen.«

zeit.title: Reality-TV: Was man aus Giftschränken rausholen kann
zeit.description: Die RTL-Show »Bad Boyfriends« hat versucht, die verhärtete Geschlechterdebatte auf Reality-TV-Niveau zu bringen. Bleiben dabei Spurenelemente von Fortschritt hängen?

zeit.title: Vereinte Nationen: UN warnen vor Aufflammen von HIV-Epidemie wegen gekürzter Gelder
zeit.description: Zuletzt sanken internationale Mittel für HIV-Programme laut UNAIDS um mehr als 1,5 Milliarden US-Dollar. Die Organisation warnt vor Rückschritten bei der HIV-Bekämpfung.

zeit.title: Wildtiere: Bären-Entwarnung im Allgäu: Spuren stammen von Dachs
Tino Sorge: Entlassener Gesundheitsstaatssekretär wirft Merz schlechten Stil vor
zeit.description: Auf seine Entlassung reagiert Tino Sorge mit schweren Vorwürfen gegen Friedrich Merz. Er hofft, dass die Entscheidung des Kanzlers »einer übergeordneten Logik folgt«.

zeit.title: Unfälle: Unfall mit Schwerverletzten - A7 Richtung Kassel gesperrt
Terror beim CSD: 4.000 bei Münchner Mahnwache nach Terroranschlag in Berlin
Personalwechsel bei CDU: Entlassener Gesundheitsstaatssekretär kritisiert Merz
Änderungen im August 2026: Warum Bahnbonus-Tickets teilweise deutlich teurer werden
zeit.description: Wer mit seinen Bahnbonuspunkten spontan Tickets bucht, muss sich umstellen. Außerdem müssen viele KI-Inhalte gekennzeichnet werden. Das ändert sich für Sie im August.

zeit.title: Bindungsangst: Ich glaube, meine Generation leidet unter einer Beziehungsphobie
zeit.description: Sie sind Single oder haben was am Laufen. Aber eine Beziehung? Monogam und so? Unsere Autorin, 17, und ihre Friends fragen sich, ob das mit der Liebe für sie gut ausgeht.

zeit.title: Auf dem Alten Markt: Hunderte in Potsdam bei Gedenken nach CSD-Anschlag

nzz.title: Andrea Pirlo wird nicht italienischer Nationalcoach – das Engagement scheitert an seinen Verbindungen zu Russland
nzz.description: Pirlos Ernennung als Commissario tecnico galt als Formsache. Doch übers Wochenende wurde die Kritik immer lauter, weil Pirlo Markenbotschafter eines russischen Wettanbieters ist.

nzz.title: Super Pumas und Feuerwehrleute: Die Schweiz schickt Verstärkung im Kampf gegen die Flammen nach Frankreich
nzz.description: Die Schweizer Einsatzkräfte reisen weitgehend autonom an. Sie bringen eigene Sanitäter, Verpflegung und Material mit, um die französischen Behörden nicht zusätzlich zu belasten.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Der Terrorist Abdul Ballout und der naive Staat: Justiz und Polizei müssen ihre Scheuklappen ablegen
nzz.description: Nur ein handlungsfähiger Rechtsstaat kann den gewaltbereiten Islamismus effektiv bekämpfen. Doch die deutsche Justiz urteilt lasch, und der Polizei wird Zurückhaltung verordnet. Das macht den Attentätern ihr Geschäft besonders leicht.

nzz.title: Neue Orte für die Weltkulturerbe-Landkarte: Unesco ehrt D-Day-Strände und südsudanesische Sümpfe
nzz.description: Die Unesco wurde als humanitäres Versprechen gegen das Vergessen und die Zerstörung ins Leben gerufen. Heute nimmt die Organisation bekannte und unbekannte Gegenden ins Weltkulturerbe auf, um auf diese aufmerksam zu machen. Was zeichnet die neuen Orte aus?

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Wo gilt das Feuer- und Feuerwerksverbot? Und wo darf die Cervelat am 1. August trotzdem auf dem Feuer brutzeln?
nzz.description: Eine Übersicht zur Lage der Nation.

nzz.title: Zwist wegen Denkmalschutz: Die Migros fordert von der Stadt Zürich mehr als 9 Millionen Franken Entschädigung
nzz.description: Die Stadt stellt die frühere Markthalle Oerlikon unter Schutz. Die Migros spricht von Enteignung. Sie hat den Fall vors Bundesgericht gezogen.

nzz.title: Der Wert einer Aktie stieg um 472 Prozent: der Mega-Börsengang des chinesischen Chipriesen CXMT
nzz.description: Mit dem zweitgrössten IPO Chinas kann CXMT den Nachfrageboom nach Speicherchips monetarisieren. Gleichzeitig besteht die Sorge, dass andere Aktien unter dem Börsengang leiden.

nzz.title: Gunther von Hagens hatte ein sehr entspanntes Verhältnis zum Tod
nzz.description: Was wäre er ohne die Toten gewesen? Nun ist der Leichenpräparator und Erfinder der «Körperwelten»-Ausstellungen mit 81 Jahren gestorben.

nzz.title: Nach dem Ja zur Individualbesteuerung wird die Heiratsstrafe erneut ein Thema
nzz.description: Bloss zwei Monate nach der kommenden September-Abstimmung muss die Schweizer Bevölkerung erneut an die Urne. Es geht um Feuerwerk, Kriegsmaterialausfuhren und – wieder einmal – um die Steuern in der Ehe.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Hitzewelle in Europa – das sind die Bilder des Rekordsommers
nzz.description: Der Sommer 2026 in Europa ist historisch heiss und trocken, mit Rekordtemperaturen von über 40 Grad Celsius.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Bei Porsche fallen 5000 Stellen weg +++ Paramount setzt Übernahme von Warner Brothers vorerst aus
Feuerpause am Golf, Eskalation am Tor der Tränen – schickt Iran jetzt seine Verbündeten los?
nzz.description: Seit Freitag herrscht zwischen Washington und Teheran eine Feuerpause. Die Huthi-Miliz in Jemen hingegen kämpft weiter. Doch die einst gefürchtete, proiranische Achse, der sie angehören, ist stark geschwächt.

nzz.title: «Dieb» und «Häftling»: Milei beschimpft Brasiliens Präsidenten Lula – und löst eine diplomatische Krise aus
nzz.description: Der argentinische Staatschef sieht das Nachbarland als Urheber einer Kampagne, die die Argentinier als ein Volk von Rassisten verunglimpfe. Nun hofft Milei, dass die «rechte Welle» auch Brasilien erfasst.

nzz.title: Manchen Kindern hilft nur noch die Abnehmspritze. Leandra verlor damit fast 20 Kilogramm
nzz.description: Abnehmspritzen werden zunehmend auch bei stark übergewichtigen Kindern und Jugendlichen eingesetzt. Erste Daten aus der Schweiz zeigen, wie wirksam sie sind – werfen aber auch Fragen nach Risiken, Kosten und einer womöglich lebenslangen Behandlung auf.

nzz.title: Der Fall Karimowa: Das Bundesstrafgericht in Bellinzona stellt das Verfahren gegen die usbekische «Prinzessin» ein
nzz.description: Die Tochter des usbekischen Diktators soll Hunderte von Millionen über Schweizer Banken gewaschen haben. Schuldig gesprochen werden aber die Bank Lombard Odier und ein ehemaliger Vermögensverwalter. Die Bank will Berufung einlegen.

spiegel.title: Ludwigshafen: Frau lässt 22 Katzen verwahrlosen – Tiere beschlagnahmt
spiegel.description: Überall Kot und Urin, dafür kein Futter oder Wasser: In einer Wohnung im Rheinland-Pfalz-Kreis beschlagnahmte das Veterinäramt 22 Katzen. Polizeiangaben zufolge sah deren Halterin die Maßnahme überhaupt nicht ein.

spiegel.title: LeBron James: Philadelphia 76ers freuen sich auf »King James«
spiegel.description: LeBron James gilt als einer der besten Basketballspieler aller Zeiten, jetzt verlässt er die Lakers und unterschreibt bei den 76ers. Der Verein hat schon mal seinen Spind dekoriert.

spiegel.title: Waldbrände in Frankreich: Evakuierte berichten von Husten und Schwindel
spiegel.description: Nur noch 15 Kilometer trennen Bordeaux von den Flammen. Der Rauch ist giftig, der Brand noch nicht unter Kontrolle. SPIEGEL-Reporterin Zoé Kammermann mit Eindrücken aus einer Evakuierungsunterkunft.

spiegel.title: Pyrocumulonimbus: Das sind die gefährlichen Feuerwolken in Frankreich
spiegel.description: Die Waldbrände bei Bordeaux erzeugen ihre eigenen Unwetter: Riesige Pyrocumulonimbus-Wolken fachen das Feuer an und lassen Blitze entstehen. Für Löschkräfte wird der Einsatz noch härter.

spiegel.title: OpenAI, Microsoft, Palantir: IT-Konzerne schmieden Sicherheitsbündnis nach KI-Angriff
spiegel.description: 30 große IT-Konzerne in den USA haben sich nach dem Angriff eines KI-Modells zu einem Sicherheitsbündnis zusammengeschlossen – darunter IBM, Microsoft und Palantir. In der Branche sorgt der Fall für Ängste.

spiegel.title: Magyar-Kandidat wird neuer Verfassungsrichter in Ungarn
spiegel.description: Ungarns Parlament hat einen neuen Verfassungsrichter gewählt. Ministerpräsident Péter Magyar ist bemüht, den Einfluss seines Vorgängers Orbán zu mindern. Amnesty International kritisiert das Verfahren.

spiegel.title: Anschlag auf den CSD Berlin: Welche Forderungen diskutiert werden
spiegel.description: Härtere Strafen, Führerscheinentzug, Aberkennung der Staatsbürgerschaft: Nach dem Anschlag auf den Berliner CSD mehren sich die Forderungen nach politischen Konsequenzen. Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Brandkatastrophe in Spanien und Frankreich: Jetzt entscheidet sich der Kampf gegen das Feuer
spiegel.description: Die Großbrände vor Madrid und Bordeaux lodern gefährlich nah an den Toren der Metropolen. Schon am Mittwoch droht die nächste Hitzewelle. Worauf es in den kommenden Stunden ankommt und wie die Lage vor Ort ist.

spiegel.title: Polen: Was das Zerwürfnis in der rechtskonservativen PiS bedeutet
spiegel.description: Vierzig Abgeordnete um Ex-Premier Mateusz Morawiecki haben die größte polnische Oppositionspartei verlassen. Nützen könnte das am Ende den Rechten.

spiegel.title: Attacke auf den CSD in Berlin: Eine Stunde vor dem Anschlag filmte das LKA Abdul B.
spiegel.description: Die Berliner Polizei hat den CSD-Attentäter Abdul B. vor dem Anschlag nach SPIEGEL-Informationen wochenlang überwacht. Beamte filmten heimlich sein Wohnhaus und hörten sein Handy ab. Terrorpläne erkannten sie nicht.

spiegel.title: Petr Pavel: Tschechiens Präsident knipst gern bei Autorennen
spiegel.description: Ja, wo fahren sie denn? Tschechiens Staatspräsident Petr Pavel war beim Großen Preis von Ungarn unterwegs. Allerdings nicht in offizieller Funktion – sondern als akkreditierter Pressefotograf.

spiegel.title: Und dann sagt der Landeschef: »Sie führen kein Unternehmen, das ist eine Partei«
spiegel.description: In der CDU wird die Kritik am Kanzler und an dessen Personalumbau immer lauter. In einer Vorstandssitzung kommt es zum offenen Schlagabtausch. Wie gefährlich ist die Lage für Friedrich Merz?

spiegel.title: CSD in Berlin: Christlich-demokratische Scheinheiligkeit nach dem Anschlag
spiegel.description: Nach dem Anschlag auf den CSD in Berlin teilen viele Politikerinnen und Politiker ihr Mitgefühl. Das wirkt bei Julia Klöckner und einigen anderen scheinheilig.

spiegel.title: Unfall auf A7: Ersthelfer von Auto erfasst
spiegel.description: Bei einem Unfall nahe Ulm eilte ein 26-Jähriger einer Frau zu Hilfe – dann wurde er selbst schwer verletzt. Er musste mit dem Hubschrauber ins Krankenhaus geflogen werden.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: Geschasster Staatssekretär Tino Sorge kritisiert Kanzler ungewöhnlich scharf
spiegel.description: Wegen seines Umgangs mit Verkehrsminister Schnieder steht Friedrich Merz bereits unter Druck. Nun meldet sich der nächste Ausgebootete: Staatssekretär Tino Sorge veröffentlicht ein bemerkenswert scharfes Statement.

spiegel.title: Anschlag auf CSD in Berlin: Hätte man die Tat verhindern können? »Auf jeden Fall«
spiegel.description: Abdul B. wurde wegen Terrorplänen von einem Gericht verurteilt, blieb aber in Freiheit. Dann steuerte er beim CSD das Auto in eine Menschenmenge. Extremismusforscher Neumann sagt: Die Justiz war zu lasch.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Feuer in Frankreich und Spanien, Patrick Schnieders Rauswurf, Attentäter Abdul B.
spiegel.description: In Frankreich und Spanien brennen die Wälder, Friedrich Merz baut sein Kabinett um und nach dem Attentat auf den CSD in Berlin wird die Schuldfrage diskutiert. Das ist die Lage am Montagabend.

spiegel.title: Rollatoren und Hörgeräte: Kosten für Versicherte gestiegen
spiegel.description: Alles wird teurer, auch Rollatoren, Hörgeräte und ähnliche Hilfsmittel. Krankenversicherungen legen nun offen, wie viel mehr Versicherte im Jahr 2025 aus eigener Tasche zahlen mussten.

observador.title: Fernando Heitor: “Como em todos os espetáculos, o melhor ...
observador.description: Fernando Heitor é coautor de “Variedades (...como uma ópera bufa erótica e satírica)”, uma peça musicada que revisita os 100 anos do teatro através de 10 personagens assíduas do Parque Mayer

observador.title: Parque com 15 hectares é "o novo pulmão" da Famalicão
observador.description: Com três miradouros, percursos pedonais e passadiços metálicos, o parque preserva um castro da Idade do Ferro classificado como Imóvel de Interesse Público.

observador.title: PCP quer regular preços dos combustíveis
observador.description: Três aumentos consecutivos empurraram gasolina e gasóleo para mais de 2€/litro. Os comunistas apontam o dedo à Galp, com 810 milhões de lucro no semestre.

observador.title: Linha da Beira Baixa deve normalizar em setembro ou outubro
observador.description: A ligação ferroviária de 240 quilómetros, afetada pelas tempestades do início do ano, deverá reabrir antes do esperado. Também a Linha do Oeste deverá ter a circulação normalizada em janeiro de 2027.

observador.title: Rússia diz estar recetiva a novas ideias de paz na Ucrânia
observador.description: São declarações da porta-voz do Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros russo. Ainda, Vladimir Putin ordenou hoje um aumento de 27 mil efetivos nas Forças Armadas.

observador.title: Putin prepara nova mobilização de até 500 mil pessoas
observador.description: O aviso é do Presidente ucraniano que cita relatórios dos serviços de informações. Zelensky afirma que o líder do Kremlin “não está preparado para parar a guerra”.

observador.title: Município da Covilhã entregou as chaves de mais 37 casas
observador.description: Investimento de 1,2 milhões de euros, financiado pelo PRR, permitiu reconstruir e reabilitar casas de mais 72 pessoas. Habitação e arrendamento acessível é outra das prioridades do município.

observador.title: Luís Neves: o ministro que não fala e o PS que o adora
observador.description: Sem entregar rendimentos, Luís Neves goza o silêncio enquanto o PS tem uma atitude "autista". Alunos sem nota e confiança no lixo? São apenas "pequenos casos", de acordo com o Governo.

observador.title: "Não se sabe quem é que manda no Irão"
observador.description: Helena Ferro Gouveia analisa o impasse entre Estados Unidos e Irão, a falta de interlocutores em Teerão e a descrença numa solução diplomática rápida para o conflito no Médio Oriente.

observador.title: As notícias das 20h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Parlamento não vai ouvir Luís Neves. AD travou audição
observador.description: IL tinha pedido para ouvir Luís Neves sobre polémicas que têm assombrado o ministro, sem sucesso. Aguiar-Branco diz que não houve consenso "inequívoco" para audição especial.

observador.title: Pauline Hanson perde recurso por discriminação racial
observador.description: A líder do One Nation fala da possibilidade de recorrer ao supremo australiano, justificando-se com a liberdade de discurso político. Hanson foi condenada por uma mensagem islamofóbica e racista.

observador.title: Fosso digital regional persiste em Portugal em 2025
observador.description: Grande Lisboa mantém "supremacia esmagadora" sobre restantes regiões. Setúbal e Região Centro têm pontuações acima da média. Investigador afirma que assimetrias são desafio na transição digital.

observador.title: 19h. Incêndio obriga ao corte da A1 nos dois sentidos
observador.description: A Autoestrada do Norte está cortada entre Albergaria e a Mealhada devido a um incêndio em Aveiro. Ainda, Donald Trump garante que os Estados Unidos tem "muitas munições" para a guerra no Irão.

observador.title: Nersant reclama apoios por desbloquear depois de tempestades
observador.description: Presidente da associação empresarial afirma que recuperação "não pode ficar limitada a linhas de crédito de baixa intensidade". Há empresas afetadas que precisam de empréstimos a fundo perdido.

observador.title: Médio Tejo recebe mais 10 milhões do Centro 2030
observador.description: Habitação acessível e habitação social são o principal alvo do investimento, mas Comunidade Intermunicipal assume que preferia reforço noutras áreas. Apoio a fundo perdido do Centro 2030 será de 25%.

observador.title: Tom Holland diz que alguns dos seus filmes são uma "merda"
observador.description: Ator britânico não especificou a que filmes se referia. Ainda assim, garantiu estar "muito orgulhoso" dos seus dois projetos mais recentes durante uma entrevista ao podcast Dish.

observador.title: Filme "A Odisseia" pirateado e publicado na rede social X
observador.description: Universal agiu rapidamente para remover filme completo de Christopher Nolan da rede de Musk (que criticou o elenco). Incidente não impede sucesso, que já conta com 550 milhões de euros na bilheteira.

letemps.description:
Alors que les flammes continuent de calciner le sud-ouest de la France, les représentants économiques locaux ont été conviés à une réunion de crise

Même si, dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi, l’incendie a été relativement plus calme – Laurent Nuñez a affirmé qu’il est «stabilisé» mais pas «fixé» –, le mégafeu qui touche la Gironde depuis plusieurs jours continue à apeurer le territoire. D

letemps.title: En France, le débat sur les feux vire au populisme
letemps.description:
ÉDITORIAL. De plus en plus notable au fur et à mesure que les cruciales élections de 2027 approchent, la violence des critiques tranche avec le besoin d’unité que devrait provoquer ce genre de drame

Les avions militaires mettent trop de temps à arriver (car les pilotes et les cales doivent être préparés): «c’est la faute à Macron». Il n’y a pas assez de canadairs (car l’Etat n’a plus d’argent

letemps.title: L’anatomiste allemand Gunther von Hagens, qui exposait des cadavres «plastinés», est décédé
letemps.description:

phys-org.title: Satellite images could help target sustainable farming support for small fields
phys-org.description: For decades, satellites have helped scientists observe Earth's changing landscapes. Now, they could also help answer one of agriculture's most pressing questions: How can the world produce more food while reducing its environmental impact?

phys-org.title: First 3D views explain how primate cone pigments distinguish red from green
phys-org.description: Human color vision depends on three types of cone cells in the retina. Although all three contain the same light-absorbing molecule, 11-cis-retinal, differences in the surrounding protein determine sensitivity to red, green or blue light. Understanding how these subtle protein differences produce such precise color discrimination has been difficult because cone pigments are highly unstable and structurally challenging to study.

phys-org.title: Soil carbon effectively measured by new, efficient AI model
phys-org.description: A new computer model is one of the first artificial intelligence tools to advance scientific discovery in agriculture and biogeochemistry and is 50 times more efficient than its predecessors, according to a study that offers a proof-of-principle for how AI might be used to shed light on obscure biological processes.

phys-org.title: Research cautions that sometimes working together can actually spur inequality
phys-org.description: Encouraging people to contribute to a common good can have a surprising drawback: a risk that rewards become concentrated among a smaller group, putting the rest at a disadvantage. Put more simply, "equality and cooperation are often in conflict," says Joshua Plotkin, Walter H. and Leonore C. Annenberg Professor of the Natural Sciences in the School of Arts & Sciences.

phys-org.title: UN lists South Sudan antelope route as heritage in danger
phys-org.description: The United Nations has fast-tracked a vast antelope migration path in South Sudan onto its List of World Heritage in Danger, the young nation's first such listing.

phys-org.title: What Australian lakes showed us about Martian hydrology
phys-org.description: The expansive red bluffs of Western Australia's Yilgarn Craton give the landscape a Martian appearance. It turns out the resemblance is more than superficial: The Yilgarn Craton also shares geological characteristics with lakes in Mars' Terra Sirenum region. T. A. Plattner and colleagues recently characterized those shared features to shed light on the region's aqueous history and its potential to have supported life in an article published in the journal Earth and Space Science.

phys-org.title: 'Dead stars' may have surprisingly healthy appetites
phys-org.description: "Dead stars" known as white dwarfs have already shown the potential to help us better understand how planetary systems, including our own solar system, take shape and evolve. Now, research from the University of Michigan and the University of Colorado Boulder suggests that potential could be even greater than anticipated.

While not uncommon, their brightness can make it difficult to accurately measure the galaxies they reside in. This means scientists must use gravitational lensing to assist in analyzing these bright objects, a method that relies on studying how an object's strong gravity bends light around its host galaxy. phys-org.title: Identify birds offline using AI: New app records animal sounds directly on your smartphone
phys-org.description: Previous apps for identifying animal calls regularly hit practical limits: Without a stable internet connection, real-time identification in forests or high mountains was impossible.

phys-org.title: Industrial poultry farming is accelerating the spread of a major foodborne disease
phys-org.description: A new study by the Ineos Oxford Institute for Antimicrobial Research at the University of Oxford reveals that industrial poultry farming has led to a more than 100-fold increase in the movement of Campylobacter, allowing strains that once circulated in wild birds to mix extensively in commercial poultry populations.

phys-org.title: Researchers uncover new mechanism behind DNA repair
phys-org.description: Roughly 20 million people receive a cancer diagnosis each year, and an estimated 1 in 5 people will receive a cancer diagnosis in their lifetime. Cancer cells arise from damage to the cell's instruction manual: DNA.

phys-org.title: Fossil footprints reveal body size and group dynamics of 1.4-million-year-old human relative
phys-org.description: Ancient footprints preserved along the shores of Kenya's Lake Turkana are reshaping scientists' understanding of one of humanity's extinct relatives. A paper published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences describes a set of fossil trackways made by a group of ancient human relatives moving along a lakeshore more than 1.4 million years ago.

phys-org.title: Gender gap in predicted grades raises questions over their use in university admissions
phys-org.description: A study of more than 350,000 students in England has found that teachers predict higher A-Level grades for girls than boys who go on to achieve the same exam results. The findings raise fresh questions about the role of predicted grades in university admissions.

phys-org.title: Hidden DNA copying may give bacteria a faster route to antibiotic resistance
phys-org.description: The dangers of antibiotic overuse have become increasingly clear in recent decades. Excessive use accelerates the evolution of bacterial resistance to antibiotics, raising the alarming prospect of infections that no longer respond to existing drugs and pose a serious threat to public health.

phys-org.title: New research turns the Dunning-Kruger effect on its head: Rethinking the confident incompetent
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Bath and The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) suggest that the celebrated Dunning-Kruger effect, often taken to mean the least competent people are the most overconfident, may actually be the wrong way around.

phys-org.title: Astronomers identify one of the universe's rarest black hole events
phys-org.description: A team of astronomers at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill has observed an extremely rare "wandering" black hole located tens of thousands of light-years from the center of its galaxy. This finding could reshape scientists' understanding of how massive black holes move through the universe after galaxies collide. The findings are published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

phys-org.title: Can a newly discovered soil fungus stop the devastating African armyworm when chemicals have failed?
phys-org.description: The African armyworm is a highly destructive migratory pest that damages maize, sorghum, millet and sugarcane. These caterpillars also cause indirect damage to livestock by destroying grazing lands and pastures.

phys-org.title: Highly tunable electro-optic isolator achieves one-way light flow on photonic chips
phys-org.description: Integrated photonic devices—tiny circuits that use light instead of electrons—are becoming increasingly important for scalable photonics technologies and high-bandwidth communications. They are particularly valuable for managing low-power, light-based data transfer inside data centers, which are needed for artificial intelligence, cloud computing and high-performance signal processing.

undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

proj-syn.title: The Cost of Not Building Data Centers
proj-syn.description: In July, New York became the first state to enact a moratorium on new data centers, a path that other states may follow. But US policymakers, drawing lessons from past failures to make economy-wide investments in electrification and rare-earth processing, should weigh the strategic costs of not building essential infrastructure.

proj-syn.title: The Dangerous Spread of Jim Crow Nostalgia
proj-syn.description: With inaccurate claims about Black Americans’ poverty and crime rates having migrated from the far-right fringe to mainstream outlets like the Wall Street Journal, it is worth considering what the data actually say. Doing so will show that there is no empirical basis for such claims, only an ideological one.

proj-syn.title: The Gulf’s Push for AI-Led Governance
proj-syn.description: Governments around the world have spent decades outsourcing their ability to think to expensive consultants, gradually ceding the knowledge and judgment needed to govern effectively. AI may now offer a way to reverse that trend, and Gulf countries are providing an early glimpse of what that may look like.

proj-syn.title: India’s Exam Worriers Become Democracy Warriors
proj-syn.description: Generations of students in India have resigned themselves to the idea that the education system is primarily a sorting mechanism, which rewards compliance. But as recent protests showed, the system's rigidity, together with insufficient rewards in the form of good jobs, has rendered this approach untenable.

proj-syn.title: Why Business Leaders Are Souring on AI
proj-syn.description: Companies have poured billions of dollars into AI in anticipation of transformative productivity gains and cost savings, but the returns have yet to justify those investments. Rising costs, intellectual-property risks, and mounting cybersecurity threats call for a more disciplined approach to AI adoption.

proj-syn.title: How Burnham Can Make UK Devolution Work
proj-syn.description: Andy Burnham’s first 100 days as prime minister of the United Kingdom will need to be devoted to building the institutional architecture for his vision of devolved governance to succeed. The question is not where to concentrate decision-making authority, but how to ensure that different authorities are working together.

proj-syn.title: West Africa Needs Its Own Draghi Moment
proj-syn.description: Senegal’s debt crisis has exposed a deeper vulnerability within West Africa’s monetary union. Unable to devalue the shared currency, member countries must either endure painful internal adjustment or boost exports to earn the foreign currency they need to repay external creditors.

proj-syn.title: Will the Real Marco Rubio Please Stand Up?
proj-syn.description: Is US Secretary of State Marco Rubio an embattled champion of Venezuelan democracy within the Trump administration, or the public face of a strategy aimed at keeping the old regime in power? Six months after Nicolás Maduro’s ouster, his record suggests democratic restoration is no longer an American priority—if it ever was.

proj-syn.title: How AI Could Reinforce Dollar Dominance
proj-syn.description: While policymakers and economists debate the future of dollar dominance, AI companies, cloud providers, and payment networks might already be writing it into the next chapter of international monetary history. Those who hope to shape that chapter must act now—or risk being left off the page.

proj-syn.title: What Ukraine’s Success Means for the West
proj-syn.description: There are several reasons why Ukraine has been able to stymie its much larger aggressor. For the world’s democracies, the most important lesson to draw from Ukrainians' doggedness and brilliant innovations and improvisations may be that we should not be so surprised.

proj-syn.title: The Strong Suffer What They Must
proj-syn.description: Foolish military interventions driven by outdated calculations of economic power have thoroughly discredited the old big powers. Thucydides might well have appreciated the irony of a world in which smaller, weaker countries like Ukraine and Iran can expose Russia and the United States, respectively, as paper tigers.

proj-syn.title: Yes, the Hong Kong of Old Is Over
proj-syn.description: The pro-China camp continues to tout Hong Kong’s resilience, recently pointing to the fact that the city has reclaimed its position as the global IPO leader. But conveniently left out of this narrative is that resilience has come to depend on the direct intervention of the Chinese authorities.

proj-syn.title: Why Iran Won’t Change
proj-syn.description: Embedded in the Islamic Republic’s foundations is a doctrine that allows for total repression of the population and mobilization of all state resources to preserve the system. This helps to explain why the US and Israel were wrong to expect the regime to change its behavior, let alone be brought down by the Iranian people.

proj-syn.title: Rethinking Global Imbalances
proj-syn.description: Today’s global imbalances, starting with China's massive trade surplus, are not simply the result of poor macroeconomic coordination. Rather, they reflect long-term strategic thinking and a departure from the bias toward openness on which the postwar trade order was built.

proj-syn.title: What the New UK Chancellor Means for the UK Economy
proj-syn.description: By appointing John Healey as chancellor of the exchequer, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has taken a calculated risk. If Healey can leverage his insider knowledge of the Treasury, pursue a bold, pro-growth agenda, and manage his defense-spending instincts, he may be able to provide the structural shake-up the UK economy needs.

proj-syn.title: Will the US Climate War with Canada Become Global?
proj-syn.description: For the first time, a great power has moved to price transboundary climate-driven harms–massive wildfires–and extract compensation unilaterally. What was previously a development, insurance, or emissions-accounting issue is now a security and trade dispute between two G7 economies, setting a precedent that others may try to follow.

proj-syn.title: America Is Closing the Door on Opportunity—and Talent
proj-syn.description: Viewed in isolation, the Trump administration's new, more restrictive student-visa policy may seem modest. But as part of a broader retreat from openness, it signals that the country once known for offering ambitious outsiders a chance to transform their lives is less willing to do so.

proj-syn.title: Large Language Models for Small Language Communities
proj-syn.description: Many developing economies cannot access large language models, most of which have been trained on datasets in English. To build scalable and inclusive LLMs for countries with minority languages, policymakers' best bet is to tap mobile network operators, with their armies of developers and data-processing capabilities.
